lehigh-2004-02.title: Pair the terms
lehigh-2004-02.body:
Group as $(1-2)+(3-4)+\cdots+(99-100)$. There are $50$ pairs, each equal to $-1$.

**Answer: $-50$**

lehigh-2004-03.title: Track the daytime height
lehigh-2004-03.body:
Each full day-night cycle gains $1$ foot. On day $n$ the frog reaches a height of $(n-1)+3=n+2$ feet before sliding back.

It reaches $20$ feet when $n+2=20$, i.e. $n=18$. It gets out during the day, so it does not slide back.

**Answer: January 18**

lehigh-2004-06.title: Compare areas
lehigh-2004-06.body:
Let the large radius be $1$. The small radii are $\frac16$ and the middle radius is $\frac13$.

Interior area: $\pi\left(\frac1{36}+\frac1{36}+\frac19\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$.

The fraction outside is $1-\frac16=\frac56$.

**Answer: $\frac56$**

lehigh-2004-07.title: Split into two trapezoids
lehigh-2004-07.body:
Place $C=(2,1)$, $D=(6,1)$, $B=(3,7)$, $A=(7,11)$, $E=(11,11)$ on the grid. The line $DE$ meets the horizontal line through $B$ at $(9,7)$.

The top piece (between heights $7$ and $11$) is a trapezoid with parallel sides $AE=4$ and $6$ (from $B$ to $(9,7)$) and height $4$: area $\frac{4(4+6)}{2}=20$.

The bottom piece (heights $1$ to $7$) has parallel sides $CD=4$ and $6$ and height $6$: area $\frac{6(4+6)}{2}=30$.

Total: $20+30=50$.

lehigh-2004-07.title: Shoelace formula
lehigh-2004-07.body:
With the vertices above, in order $A,B,C,D,E$: $\frac12|\sum(x_iy_{i+1}-x_{i+1}y_i)|=\frac12|(7\cdot7-3\cdot11)+(3\cdot1-2\cdot7)+(2\cdot1-6\cdot1)+(6\cdot11-11\cdot1)+(11\cdot11-7\cdot11)|=\frac12|16-11-4+55+44|=50$.

**Answer: 50**

lehigh-2004-09.title: Difference of two squares
lehigh-2004-09.body:
$|x|+|y|\le r$ is a diamond (square) with diagonals $2r$, area $2r^2$.

For $r=2$: area $8$. For $r=1$: area $2$.

The region between them has area $8-2=6$.

**Answer: 6**

lehigh-2004-10.title: Forced cells
lehigh-2004-10.body:
Bottom row: it has $1$ and $4$, and column 2 already has a $2$, so it reads $1,3,2,4$.

Column 4 has $1$ and $4$, so rows 2 and 3 hold $2,3$ there; row 2 already has a $2$, so row 2 ends in $3$ and row 3 ends in $2$.

Row 2 is now $\_,2,\_,3$ and needs $1,4$; column 1 has a $1$ at the bottom, so row 2 is $4,2,1,3$.

Column 1 contains $4,1$; row 3 starts with $2$ or $3$ but row 3 ends in $2$, so row 3 starts with $3$. Row 3 is $3,\_,x,2$ needing $1,4$ in the middle. Column 3 already has $1$ (row 2), so $x=4$ (and column 2 gets $1$).

$$\begin{array}{cccc}2&4&3&1\\4&2&1&3\\3&1&4&2\\1&3&2&4\end{array}$$

**Answer: 4**

lehigh-2004-11.title: Equation for the total
lehigh-2004-11.body:
Let $x$ be the number of students including Johnny. The other $x-1$ students had total $71(x-1)$, so
$$71(x-1)+96=72x\implies x=96-71=25.$$
**Answer: 25**

lehigh-2004-11.title: Compare with the new average
lehigh-2004-11.body:
Johnny's $96$ is $24$ above the new average $72$. The other students average $71$, which is $1$ below the new average, so each of them is a deficit of $1$. The surplus $24$ exactly cancels the deficits of $24$ other students. With Johnny that is $25$ students.

**Answer: 25**

lehigh-2004-12.title: Split along BE
lehigh-2004-12.body:
Triangle $ABE$ is an isosceles right triangle with hypotenuse $BE=2$, so its legs are $\sqrt2$ and its area is $\frac12\cdot\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2=1$.

$BCDE$ is an isosceles trapezoid with $BE=2$, legs $1$ and $CD=1$. Each leg is offset horizontally by $\frac{2-1}{2}=\frac12$, so the height is $\sqrt{1-\frac14}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$. Its area is $\frac{2+1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}$.

Total: $1+\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}$.

**Answer: $1+\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}$**

lehigh-2004-14.title: Double root
lehigh-2004-14.body:
Since $f\ge 0$ everywhere and $f(1)=0$, the parabola touches the axis at $x=1$, so $f(x)=a(x-1)^2$.

$f(3)=4a=3$ gives $a=\frac34$. Then $f(5)=\frac34\cdot16=12$.

**Answer: 12**

lehigh-2004-15.title: Right triangle
lehigh-2004-15.body:
Initially the string hangs doubled, so the bead is $13$ inches below her hands. After rising $8$ inches it is $5$ inches below the level of her hands.

The bead hangs midway between the hands, and each half of the string still has length $13$. Each half is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with vertical leg $5$, so the horizontal leg is $\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12$.

The hands are $2\cdot12=24$ inches apart.

**Answer: 24 inches**

lehigh-2004-17.title: Take square roots
lehigh-2004-17.body:
The fraction equals $1$ or $-1$.

If it equals $1$: $a(1-b)=b(1-a)\Rightarrow a=b$, which is excluded.

If it equals $-1$: $a(1-b)=-b(1-a)\Rightarrow a-ab=-b+ab\Rightarrow a+b=2ab$.

Hence $\frac{a+b}{ab}=2$.

**Answer: 2**

lehigh-2004-18.title: Angle chase
lehigh-2004-18.body:
Let $\angle CFE=x$, $\angle ADE=\angle AED=y$ (isosceles), and each half of angle $C$ equal $z$. Let $G$ be where $CF$ meets $AB$.

Triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$ share the angle at $A$, so $180-2y=180-40-2z$, i.e. $y=z+20$.

In triangles $DFG$ and $BCG$ the angles at $G$ are vertical, so $\angle FDG+x=\angle B+\angle GCB$ (the third angles are equal). Here $\angle FDG=\angle ADE=y$ (vertical angles) and $\angle GCB=z$, so $x+y=40+z$.

Substituting $y=z+20$: $x+z+20=40+z$, so $x=20$.

**Answer: 20 degrees**

lehigh-2004-20.title: Vieta's formulas
lehigh-2004-20.body:
$\frac1{ab}+\frac1{ac}+\frac1{bc}=\frac{c+b+a}{abc}$.

By Vieta, $a+b+c=2$ and $abc=-8$. So the value is $\frac{2}{-8}=-\frac14$.

**Answer: $-\frac14$**

lehigh-2004-21.title: Factor
lehigh-2004-21.body:
The inequality is $n^4-6n^3-n^2+6n<0$, i.e. $n(n-6)(n-1)(n+1)<0$.

A product of four distinct linear factors with roots $-1,0,1,6$ is negative between consecutive roots alternately: negative on $(-1,0)$ and on $(1,6)$, positive elsewhere.

The first interval contains no integer; the second contains $n=2,3,4,5$.

**Answer: 4**

lehigh-2004-22.title: Right triangle
lehigh-2004-22.body:
With $O$ the origin, $OQ\perp PQ$, $OQ=2$ and $OP=8$. So $PQ=\sqrt{8^2-2^2}=\sqrt{60}=2\sqrt{15}$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{15}$**

lehigh-2004-23.title: Bound $a$
lehigh-2004-23.body:
From the first equation $a^3=b^3+c^3+3abc$ exceeds both $b^3$ and $c^3$, so $a$ is the largest of the three numbers.

Hence $b+c<2a$, and the second equation gives $a^2=2(b+c)<4a$, so $a<4$. Also $a^2$ is even, so $a$ is even, so $a=2$.

Then $b+c=2$, so $b=c=1$. Check: $8-1-1=6=3\cdot2\cdot1\cdot1$. ✓

**Answer: $(a,b,c)=(2,1,1)$**

lehigh-2004-23.title: Use the factorization
lehigh-2004-23.body:
For $x=a,\ y=-b,\ z=-c$ the identity $x^3+y^3+z^3-3xyz=(x+y+z)\cdot\tfrac12\left[(x-y)^2+(y-z)^2+(z-x)^2\right]$ gives
$$a^3-b^3-c^3-3abc=(a-b-c)\cdot\tfrac12\left[(a+b)^2+(b-c)^2+(a+c)^2\right].$$
The bracket is positive, so $a=b+c$. Then $a^2=2a$, so $a=2$ and $b=c=1$.

**Answer: $(2,1,1)$**

lehigh-2004-24.title: Factor the difference
lehigh-2004-24.body:
Let $p+q=a^2$, $p+7q=b^2$. Then $6q=b^2-a^2=(b-a)(b+a)$.

The two factors have the same parity and their product is even, so both are even and $4\mid 6q$; hence $q$ is even and $q=2$.

Then $(b-a)(b+a)=12$ with both factors even: $(2,6)$, so $b=4$, $a=2$. Then $p=a^2-q=4-2=2$ (check: $2+2=4$, $2+14=16$).

So the only such prime is $p=2$.

**Answer: 2**

lehigh-2004-25.title: Angle sum
lehigh-2004-25.body:
Let $v$ be the number of interior vertices. By the edge-to-edge condition, no vertex lies in the middle of another triangle's edge, so the angles around each interior vertex sum to $360^\circ$, while the four corners of the square contribute $4\cdot90^\circ=360^\circ$.

The angle sum of all $30$ triangles is $30\cdot180^\circ$, so
$$30\cdot180=360v+360\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 30=2v+2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v=14.$$

**Answer: 14**

lehigh-2004-26.title: Complement
lehigh-2004-26.body:
There are $9000$ four-digit numbers. Those with all digits distinct: $9$ choices for the first digit (nonzero), then $9$ for the second (anything but the first), $8$ for the third, $7$ for the fourth: $9\cdot9\cdot8\cdot7=4536$.

So $9000-4536=4464$.

**Answer: 4464**

lehigh-2004-27.title: Factor pairs
lehigh-2004-27.body:
$(x+y)(x-y)=1001=7\cdot11\cdot13$. Both factors are odd, so $x=\frac{(x+y)+(x-y)}2$ and $y$ are integers. The pairs $(x+y,x-y)$ with $x+y>x-y>0$ are $(1001,1),(143,7),(91,11),(77,13)$, and each gives positive $y$.

$x$-values: $501,\ 75,\ 51,\ 45$. Sum: $501+75+51+45=672$.

**Answer: 672**

lehigh-2004-28.title: Law of cosines
lehigh-2004-28.body:
The side $s_2=9$ is opposite the $60^\circ$ angle, so
$$81=100+x^2-2\cdot10\cdot x\cos60^\circ=100+x^2-10x,$$
i.e. $x^2-10x+19=0$, so $x=5\pm\sqrt6$ (both positive).

The difference is $2\sqrt6$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt6$**

lehigh-2004-30.title: Distance to the center
lehigh-2004-30.body:
Place the center of the arc at $O=(0,0)$ and the square $[0,4]^2$. The small circle (radius $r$) is tangent to the top and right sides, so its center is $(4-r,4-r)$, at distance $\sqrt2(4-r)$ from $O$.

It is externally tangent to the arc of radius $4$, so this distance is $4+r$:
$$\sqrt2(4-r)=4+r\ \Rightarrow\ r(\sqrt2+1)=4(\sqrt2-1)\ \Rightarrow\ r=4(\sqrt2-1)^2=12-8\sqrt2.$$

**Answer: $12-8\sqrt2$**

lehigh-2004-35.title: Area condition
lehigh-2004-35.body:
The other leg is $\sqrt{100-y^2}$, so the area is $\frac12y\sqrt{100-y^2}>15$, i.e. $y^2(100-y^2)>900$, i.e. $y^4-100y^2+900<0$.

The roots in $y^2$ are $10$ and $90$, so $10<y^2<90$, i.e. $\sqrt{10}<y<3\sqrt{10}$ (both within $[0,10]$).

The probability is $\frac{3\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{10}}{10}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt{10}}5$**

lehigh-2004-36.title: Factor the sum
lehigh-2004-36.body:
Every such integer is uniquely $2^i3^j$ with $i,j\ge0$. So the sum is
$$\sum_{i,j\ge0}\frac1{2^i3^j}=\left(\sum_i\frac1{2^i}\right)\left(\sum_j\frac1{3^j}\right)=\frac1{1-\frac12}\cdot\frac1{1-\frac13}=2\cdot\frac32=3.$$

**Answer: 3**

lehigh-2004-37.title: Factoring trick
lehigh-2004-37.body:
For $x,y\ne0$: $2(x+y)=xy\iff(x-2)(y-2)=4$.

Integer factor pairs of $4$: $(1,4),(2,2),(4,1),(-1,-4),(-4,-1),(-2,-2)$. These give $(x,y)=(3,6),(4,4),(6,3),(1,-2),(-2,1),(0,0)$. The last has $x=0$, which is not allowed.

That leaves $5$ pairs.

**Answer: 5**

lehigh-2004-38.title: Rewrite the product
lehigh-2004-38.body:
$\prod_{i=2}^n(i^2-1)=\prod_{i=2}^n(i-1)(i+1)=(n-1)!\cdot\frac{(n+1)!}{2}=\big((n-1)!\big)^2\cdot\frac{n(n+1)}{2}.

This is a perfect square iff $\frac{n(n+1)}2$ is a perfect square. For $n=2,\dots,7$ it equals $3,6,10,15,21,28$, none a square; for $n=8$ it is $36=6^2$.

**Answer: 8**

lehigh-2004-40.title: Coordinates
lehigh-2004-40.body:
Stretch the picture vertically by a factor $\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$ (this changes all areas by the same factor, so ratios of areas are unchanged). With $AB=3$:
$$A=(0,0),\ B=(3,0),\ C=(\tfrac32,\tfrac32),\ F=(1,0),\ D=(\tfrac52,\tfrac12),\ E=(1,1).$$
The lines $AD$, $BE$, $CF$ meet pairwise at
$$AD\cap CF=(\tfrac{15}{14},\tfrac3{14}),\quad AD\cap BE=(\tfrac{15}7,\tfrac37),\quad BE\cap CF=(\tfrac97,\tfrac67).$$
Their triangle has area $\frac9{28}$ (shoelace), while $[ABC]=\frac12\cdot3\cdot\frac32=\frac94$.

The ratio is $\frac{9/4}{9/28}=7$. (This also follows from Routh's theorem.)

**Answer: 7**
